behaviour: Plumb confirms records without the owner's words only through the calibrated judge; settling by context does not exist.
note: Settling by context removed; calibration by trial cards kept.

behaviour: The diagram mod lives in its own repository beside plumb and draws architecture-diagram skill output as SVG or box-drawing text.
A card can carry an optional block diagram that the agent draws and the card renders beside its question.
note: Drawing code lives once in diagram mod.

behaviour: The clarify question the hook prints shows only the topic, question and options, not the read-back's will, won't or assumed lines.
note: Possibly overlaps later card-content rules (INT-049, INT-070).

behaviour: Plumb offers commands to remove a link from a record and to move a link to a new target, neither of which confirms anything.
Conflicts are answered on cards drawn by the one card renderer or by the owner's typed choose, with no agent relay.
note: Finishing card-redesign leftovers; durable parts restated elsewhere.

behaviour: Plumb tests avoid repeated cache, progress and lock-file access while preserving log integrity.
note: Specific performance fix in a worktree.

behaviour: Plumb raises a card only for requests about the system being built, not for operating Claude Code or the machine.
note: Request check later limited to typed clarify.

behaviour: The card pane lets the owner step through waiting cards and diagrams, opens only on click, and asks to dock on the right.
The agent may suggest a conflict resolution when confident, shown first as recommended, but only the owner's choice applies it.
Cards live on the panel and the end-of-turn text prints only one short plumb status line of what changed.
note: Full cards printed only where panel cannot run.

behaviour: An answered card leaves the waiting list at once and the panel groups cards by state.
The owner interviews on the best browser UI for resolving plumb issues before building anything.
The first browser product is an issue-resolution workspace linking agent activity to issues, not agent lifecycle management.
The browser workspace works on one project at a time and resolves every issue type, leaving team coordination to the agent harness.
note: Answering an issue differs from completing repairs.

behaviour: The owner asks to challenge whether a coding agent should handle resolutions inside the browser UI.
note: Exploratory; outcome not stated in this text.

behaviour: The browser keeps the existing cards-and-mods behaviour as its baseline for answering issues and agent follow-up.
note: Same autonomy policy; only presentation improves.

behaviour: Plumb withdraws a card by itself when its question stops standing, without the owner asking for clean-up.
When the owner clearly answers a question put to them, plumb records the answer as intent without re-asking on a new card.
note: Possibly narrowed by INT-059 and INT-060.

behaviour: Plumb catches stale links, overlapping requirements and unmarked changes while work happens instead of afterwards.
note: Also asks one-off cleanup of today's stale links.

behaviour: Only what plumb saw itself counts as the owner's answer; the agent never carries it, and cards are raised before the answer.
note: Press, typed command, or own message read by plumb.

behaviour: Plumb analyses a request only when the owner types /plumb clarify; ordinary messages run no request check.
note: Intent loop opened on command refines this.

behaviour: Plumb asks the owner a principle once and settles the detailed cards that hinge on it from that decision.
note: Few high-level cards; background job settles.

behaviour: Build the browser issue workspace with diagrams using a workflow of subagents and real-API tests.
Resume and finish the browser issue workspace task through a workflow, fixing four queued defects.
Hook hard limit and soft budgets are configurable settings with higher defaults so checks are not skipped.
The verdict judge asks JEV first and uses its verdict above the calibrated zero-false-accept threshold, else the judge model.
The browser workspace's Python tests are excluded from the default pytest run and run only on request.
Open verdict and proof items are resolved by principles; partly answered judge jobs apply existing verdicts and leave the rest waiting.
note: Never decides unanswered parts by rule.

behaviour: The clarifier asks every blocking question, each specific, through Claude Code's question tool rather than cards.
note: Overlaps INT-070 on question tool use.

behaviour: The judge reads the owner's whole logged words wherever plumb runs, including worktrees, and says when it had only the quote.
Cards are reserved for complex decisions with trade-offs; other questions use the question tool and recorded intent is applied first.
Plumb's background processes on Windows open no console window for themselves or their commands.
All hook time limits are raised so a hook is cut only when truly stuck, including watchdog, budgets and host timeouts.
Plumb works as an intent loop opened on command, clarifying with the question tool and passing a judge gate before building.
